newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank seen cutting discount rate soon.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank seen cutting discount rate soon.

text.p: Thai Bankers Assocation chief Olarn Chaiprawat said on Wednesday the Bank of Thailand was likely to cut its discount rate in the next couple of days to trigger interest rates cuts by commercial banks.
"The central bank is expected to cut the discount rate from the current level of 10.50 percent in the next couple of days or by the end of next week," Olarn told reporters.
But he did not say how much of a cut was expected.

The discount rate is the interest rate charged to commercial banks on loans from the Bank of Thailand. It currently stands at 10.50 percent. The last time the central bank cut the discount rate was on March 1, 1995.
After the central bank's discount rate reduction, the commercial banks would cut their lending rates by about 25 to 50 basis points, Olarn said.

Bank of Thailand officials on Wednesday said the bank did not plan to cut the rate on Wednesday, but did not say if or when it might make a cut which has been widely anticipated by the financial community.
